quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Hi team, the meeting notes from yesterday ___ attached below for your reference.
quests.completedSentence: Hi team, the meeting notes from yesterday are attached below for your reference.
quests.grammarRule: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The meeting notes' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Notes' already sounds plural - check the noun that's really doing the action.
quests.example: Hi team, the meeting notes from yesterday are attached below for your reference.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Please note that each department ___ required to submit its budget by Friday.
quests.completedSentence: Please note that each department is required to submit its budget by Friday.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each department' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Think about how 'each' presents the department: as a group, or one at a time?
quests.example: Please note that each department is required to submit its budget by Friday.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The client, along with two of his colleagues, ___ joining our call at 3 PM.
quests.completedSentence: The client, along with two of his colleagues, is joining our call at 3 PM.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the client', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'along with two of his colleagues' adds detail, but it doesn't create a second subject.
quests.example: The client, along with two of his colleagues, is joining our call at 3 PM.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Every student ___ required to submit a rough draft before the final essay.
quests.completedSentence: Every student is required to submit a rough draft before the final essay.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Every student' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Ask whether 'every' looks at the students collectively or one by one.
quests.example: Every student is required to submit a rough draft before the final essay.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Agreement follows the head noun before an 'of' phrase, not the noun within it
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The list of assignments due this week ___ posted on the classroom portal.
quests.completedSentence: The list of assignments due this week is posted on the classroom portal.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before an 'of' phrase, not the noun within it
quests.ruleExplanation: The head noun is 'the list', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on 'the list', not the assignments listed inside it.
quests.example: The list of assignments due this week is posted on the classroom portal.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the schedule change for the exam.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the teacher nor the students are aware of the schedule change for the exam.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb follows the nearer noun. 'The students' sits closest to the verb and is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: With 'neither...nor', check the noun closest to the verb.
quests.example: Neither the teacher nor the students are aware of the schedule change for the exam.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Percentage + 'of' + plural noun takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Sixty percent of the survey respondents ___ satisfied with the new policy.
quests.completedSentence: Sixty percent of the survey respondents are satisfied with the new policy.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + plural noun takes a plural verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Respondents' is countable and plural, so 'sixty percent of the survey respondents' takes a plural verb: 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether 'respondents' can be counted individually - that decides the verb.
quests.example: Sixty percent of the survey respondents are satisfied with the new policy.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The number of complaints received each quarter ___ steadily.
quests.completedSentence: The number of complaints received each quarter declines steadily.
quests.grammarRule: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The number of complaints' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'declines'.
quests.nativeTip: Is this sentence about the complaints themselves, or about the count of them?
quests.example: The number of complaints received each quarter declines steadily.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Collective noun 'committee' takes a singular verb when acting as one unit
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The committee, after reviewing all the data, ___ its final recommendation next week.
quests.completedSentence: The committee, after reviewing all the data, presents its final recommendation next week.
quests.grammarRule: Collective noun 'committee' takes a singular verb when acting as one unit
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The committee' is a singular collective noun, so the verb takes -s: 'presents'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase about reviewing data is just extra detail about the committee.
quests.example: The committee, after reviewing all the data, presents its final recommendation next week.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is plural
quests.sentenceWithBlank: There ___ two flights available on Tuesday morning.
quests.completedSentence: There are two flights available on Tuesday morning.
quests.grammarRule: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is plural
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Two flights' is plural, so the sentence uses 'there are'.
quests.nativeTip: Check the noun that follows 'there' to decide between 'is' and 'are'.
quests.example: There are two flights available on Tuesday morning.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The train that departs at 9 AM ___ three stops before reaching downtown.
quests.completedSentence: The train that departs at 9 AM makes three stops before reaching downtown.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.ruleExplanation: The main subject is 'the train', which is singular. The verb takes -s: 'makes'.
quests.nativeTip: 'That departs at 9 AM' describes the train - it doesn't change what the main verb agrees with.
quests.example: The train that departs at 9 AM makes three stops before reaching downtown.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Each guest ___ asked to arrive fifteen minutes before the ceremony begins.
quests.completedSentence: Each guest is asked to arrive fifteen minutes before the ceremony begins.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each guest' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Consider whether 'each' looks at the guests together or one by one.
quests.example: Each guest is asked to arrive fifteen minutes before the ceremony begins.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Your order, along with a free gift, ___ on its way to you.
quests.completedSentence: Your order, along with a free gift, is on its way to you.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'your order', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The free gift mentioned after 'along with' doesn't add a second subject.
quests.example: Your order, along with a free gift, is on its way to you.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Several' / 'many' takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Several updates ___ available for your device.
quests.completedSentence: Several updates are available for your device.
quests.grammarRule: 'Several' / 'many' takes a plural verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Several updates' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Think about whether 'several' points to one item or more than one.
quests.example: Several updates are available for your device.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Third-person singular subject in the simple present
quests.sentenceWithBlank: This app ___ your location to provide accurate recommendations.
quests.completedSentence: This app uses your location to provide accurate recommendations.
quests.grammarRule: Third-person singular subject in the simple present
quests.ruleExplanation: 'This app' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'uses'.
quests.nativeTip: Look at 'this app' - how many things is the sentence describing?
quests.example: This app uses your location to provide accurate recommendations.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Everyone entering this facility ___ a visitor badge.
quests.completedSentence: Everyone entering this facility needs a visitor badge.
quests.grammarRule: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everyone' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'needs'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Everyone' refers to many people - but how does the word itself behave grammatically?
quests.example: Everyone entering this facility needs a visitor badge.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The elevator on the left ___ currently out of service.
quests.completedSentence: The elevator on the left is currently out of service.
quests.grammarRule: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The elevator' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'On the left' just tells us which elevator - it doesn't change the subject's number.
quests.example: The elevator on the left is currently out of service.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Compound subject joined by 'and' takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Visitors and staff ___ both required to sign in at the front desk.
quests.completedSentence: Visitors and staff are both required to sign in at the front desk.
quests.grammarRule: Compound subject joined by 'and' takes a plural verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Visitors and staff' is a compound subject joined by 'and', so it's plural. The verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Two different groups joined by 'and' always form a plural subject.
quests.example: Visitors and staff are both required to sign in at the front desk.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the refund nor the replacement ___ available until Monday.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the refund nor the replacement is available until Monday.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the replacement', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: With 'neither...nor', match the verb to the noun closest to it.
quests.example: Neither the refund nor the replacement is available until Monday.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The team that handles billing issues ___ back to you within 24 hours.
quests.completedSentence: The team that handles billing issues gets back to you within 24 hours.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.ruleExplanation: The main subject is 'the team', a singular collective noun. The verb takes -s: 'gets'.
quests.nativeTip: 'That handles billing issues' describes the team - it doesn't change the main verb's agreement.
quests.example: The team that handles billing issues gets back to you within 24 hours.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: A number of customers ___ reported the same issue this week.
quests.completedSentence: A number of customers have reported the same issue this week.
quests.grammarRule: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'A number of customers' means 'several customers', so the verb is 'have'.
quests.nativeTip: Compare 'a number of' with 'the number of' - which meaning applies here?
quests.example: A number of customers have reported the same issue this week.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The software, along with its latest updates, ___ compatible with older devices.
quests.completedSentence: The software, along with its latest updates, remains compatible with older devices.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the software', which is singular. The verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.nativeTip: The updates mentioned after 'along with' don't add a second subject.
quests.example: The software, along with its latest updates, remains compatible with older devices.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Each of the settings ___ customizable in the new version.
quests.completedSentence: Each of the settings is customizable in the new version.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each of the settings' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Which word is the actual subject: 'each' or the noun after 'of'?
quests.example: Each of the settings is customizable in the new version.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The files that sync across devices ___ encrypted for security.
quests.completedSentence: The files that sync across devices are encrypted for security.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.ruleExplanation: The main subject is 'the files', which is plural. The verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: 'That sync across devices' describes the files - focus on the true plural subject instead.
quests.example: The files that sync across devices are encrypted for security.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The airline that operates this route ___ known for its punctuality.
quests.completedSentence: The airline that operates this route is known for its punctuality.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.ruleExplanation: The main subject is 'the airline', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'That operates this route' describes the airline - it doesn't change the main subject's number.
quests.example: The airline that operates this route is known for its punctuality.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is plural
quests.sentenceWithBlank: There ___ several delays reported at the airport this morning.
quests.completedSentence: There are several delays reported at the airport this morning.
quests.grammarRule: 'There' + 'are' when the subject that follows is plural
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Several delays' is plural, so the sentence uses 'there are'.
quests.nativeTip: Check the noun after 'there' to decide between 'is' and 'are'.
quests.example: There are several delays reported at the airport this morning.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Either the train or the bus ___ a good option for reaching the city center.
quests.completedSentence: Either the train or the bus is a good option for reaching the city center.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the bus', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: With 'either...or', focus on the noun closest to the verb.
quests.example: Either the train or the bus is a good option for reaching the city center.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The clinic, along with two nearby pharmacies, ___ closed on public holidays.
quests.completedSentence: The clinic, along with two nearby pharmacies, is closed on public holidays.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'the clinic', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The nearby pharmacies mentioned after 'along with' don't add a second subject.
quests.example: The clinic, along with two nearby pharmacies, is closed on public holidays.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Money expressed as a single total amount takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Twenty dollars ___ the co-pay for this visit.
quests.completedSentence: Twenty dollars is the co-pay for this visit.
quests.grammarRule: Money expressed as a single total amount takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Twenty dollars' is treated as one total amount, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Is the sentence talking about twenty separate dollars or one total amount?
quests.example: Twenty dollars is the co-pay for this visit.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Everyone in the group chat ___ excited about the reunion next month.
quests.completedSentence: Everyone in the group chat seems excited about the reunion next month.
quests.grammarRule: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everyone' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.nativeTip: One last check: how does 'everyone' behave, however many people it covers?
quests.example: Everyone in the group chat seems excited about the reunion next month.
